First release of **cloak**: a mounted drive where you see your real files, while
the folder on disk holds them under dull machine-looking names with only the
first and last bytes of each file encrypted. Obfuscation, not full encryption
— see the threat model in the README.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.1.0-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon + Intel) | `cloak-v0.1.0-macos-universal.zip` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

Each zip has `cloak` (CLI), `cloak-gui` (desktop app) and the mount adapter
(`cloak-winmount.exe` on Windows, `cloak-mount` on macOS). Keep them in the
same folder: the app launches the adapter from next to itself.

The binaries are not code-signed. On macOS, clear the download quarantine
before first run: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine cloak-v0.1.0-macos-universal`.

## Highlights

- **One drive on Windows and macOS.** A store folder (synced or copied) mounts
  the same on both: accented names agree (NFC/NFD), matching is
  case-insensitive with full Unicode folding, and characters only macOS allows
  (`: ? " < > | * \`, trailing dots, `CON`…) show on Windows through the same
  look-alike mapping macOS's SMB client uses. Names that can't exist on both
  are refused.
- **Live refresh in Explorer and Directory Opus** on Windows: new and renamed
  items appear immediately, no F5.
- **Normal app saves work**: rename-over-existing, case-only renames,
  `ReplaceFile`, flush, timestamp/attribute updates and date-preserving copies.
- **Folders on macOS**: the macOS adapter handles the full folder tree,
  keeps Finder's `._*` / `.DS_Store` files out of the store, and unmounts
  cleanly when a drive is locked.
- **Safe deletes on Windows**: deleting a non-empty folder without recursion is
  refused, as on NTFS.

## Known limitations

- **The macOS mount is new and has not yet been tested on a real Mac.** It
  builds and the shared engine is fully tested, but treat it as a preview and
  keep a backup of anything you put in a drive.
- FUSE-T is not supported yet (macFUSE only).
- File timestamps are not stored: they show as 1601 on Windows and 1970 on
  macOS.
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
